questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Designing a scalable tenant isolation guard is critical for security in shared clusters. This question tests practical policy construction and verification end-to-end.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext norms (runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
- Pod security and network isolation (NetworkPolicy, default-deny)
- StorageClass encryption and tenant scoping
- Kyverno as admission policy and CI gate integration

## Code Example

```yaml
# Failing manifest (missing readOnlyRootFilesystem)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/svc-a:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
# should also include readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and non-hostNetwork
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (required fields present)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/svc-a:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      hostNetwork: false
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the policy across dozens of tenants? 
- How would you monitor non-compliant clusters in production?

## Why This Is Asked
Beginners must apply concrete security defaults to container specs, learn how policies gate PRs, and validate locally and in CI.

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes securityContext fields
- Kyverno policy syntax and testing
- CI gate integration in GitHub Actions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-sec-context
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: require-sec-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment","StatefulSet","DaemonSet","Job","CronJob"]
    validate:
      message: "Containers must run as non-root with readOnlyRootFilesystem and drop ALL capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this policy for InitContainers? 
- How would you measure policy coverage over time (e.g., CI reports, dashboards)?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses practical CI gating, SBOM generation, and license compliance in a mono-repo.

- SBOM generation with Syft
- SPDX license checks and whitelisting
- Per-service CI gates in a mono-repo
- Interpreting SBOM/license failures

## Code Example
```yaml
name: SBOM and License Gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          echo "build service image"
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft image:myorg/service:sha -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Upload SBOM
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sbom.json
          path: sbom.json
      - name: License check
        run: |
          if on_disallowed_license; then exit 1; fi
```

- How would you auto-fix or report to maintainers?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Real-world security requires automated SBOMs and multi-tool vulnerability checks to prevent risky images from entering registries.

## Key Concepts
- SBOM generation with Syft
- Parallel scans with Trivy and Grype
- PR gating and artifact attachment
- Validation in CI and via PR comments

## Code Example
```yaml
# minimal GitHub Actions workflow (yaml)
name: SBOM and vulnerability gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          docker build -t myimage:${{ github.sha }} .
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock anchore/syft:latest DockerImage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > sbom.json
      - name: Scan with Trivy
        run: |
          docker run --rm -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock aquasecurity/trivy:latest image --exit-code 1 --no-progress myimage:${{ github.sha }} || true
      - name: Scan with Grype
        run: |
          grype myimage:${{ github.sha }} -o json > grype.json || true
      - name: Upload SBOMs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: sboms
          path: sbom.json, grype.json
      - name: Fail if CVEs found
        run: |
          if [ -s grype.json ] && grep -q '"score": 7' grype.json; then exit 1; fi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this gate for a multi-arch build?
- How would you integrate SBOM attestation into your registry metadata?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to enforce secure secret handling across multi-cloud clusters, using policy-as-code, and integrating cert-manager with GitOps pipelines.

## Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA)
- cert-manager Certificate -> Secret flow
- ExternalSecret / SecretStore integration
- CI gating and canary verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno policy (example)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-inline-tls-and-enforce-secretref
spec:
  validationFailureAction: fail
  rules:
  - name: deny-inline-tls
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "TLS data must come from cert-manager SecretRef; do not inline certificates"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              volumes:
              - secret:
                  secretName: "?!*"
```

```rego
# OPA/ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (illustrative)
package kubernetes.admission

deny[{"msg":"inline certs not allowed"}] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment" or input.request.kind.kind == "StatefulSet"
  some i
  secret := input.request.object.spec.template.spec.volumes[i]
  secret.secretName != "" # ensure SecretRef used, not inline data
}
```
